query: For a high-entropy alloy initially designed as a single-phase solid solution, what testable mechanistic hypothesis explains whether and why it loses toughness or undergoes brittle fracture under mechanical loading in demanding engineering service? Define a controlled comparison that would reveal the governing behavior, predict observations relative to the initial baseline, identify the applicable service and loading boundaries, cite supporting prior evidence, and state a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Thermal aging of an initially single-phase FCC CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy induces nanoscale B2-rich intermetallic precipitation at grain boundaries, which lowers cohesive boundary strength and promotes intergranular brittle fracture under mechanical loading, thereby reducing overall toughness.
generation.material_initial_state: Solution-annealed, single-phase FCC equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloy with K_IC ≈100 MPa√m and predominantly ductile transgranular fracture.
generation.conditions: Compact-tension fracture toughness tests at room temperature, load-line displacement rate 10⁻³ mm/s, ΔK range 10–30 MPa√m.
generation.structural_mediator: Nanoscale B2-rich intermetallic precipitates decorating grain boundaries.
generation.mechanism: Precipitates act as crack nucleation sites and reduce grain-boundary cohesive strength, shifting fracture mode from ductile transgranular to brittle intergranular.
generation.predicted_outcome: Aged specimens exhibit ≥30% reduction in K_IC relative to baseline and fracture surfaces with ≥50% intergranular features.
generation.baseline: As-annealed alloy with K_IC ≈100 MPa√m and ductile transgranular fracture.
generation.boundary: Applies for thermal exposures between 500 °C and 700 °C and loading rates between 10⁻⁴ and 10⁻² mm/s.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate uncertainty in precipitate volume fraction and exact embrittlement magnitude.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of C(T) specimens from the same batch: one as-annealed, one aged at 600 °C for 100 h. Perform fracture toughness tests and microstructural analysis (TEM/SEM) of grain-boundary precipitates and fracture surfaces.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If aged specimens show <10% change in K_IC and grain-boundary precipitate volume fraction remains <1%, the hypothesis is falsified.
